title: Remove global execution settings UI; add per-case run/trace and run-all buttons
description:
## Summary

After PR 243 (PLAT-c6g6.3) lands, the global execution settings UI in CodeEditor (stdin, random_seed, attached_files) exists solely to support trace debugging. This is wasteful and confusing — students must configure settings globally when they should be acting on individual test cases.

## Desired UX

1. **Per-case actions**: Each test case in CasesPanel gets its own Run and Trace (debug) buttons. Running uses that case's stdin/random_seed/files. Tracing launches the debugger with the same inputs.
2. **"Run All" button**: A single action to execute all test cases at once (existing bulk execute behavior).
3. **Remove global execution settings UI**: The legacy stdin/random_seed/attached_files panel in CodeEditor is removed entirely. All execution inputs are defined per-case.

## Clean up global execution settings vestiges

Remove all remaining traces of the global execution settings pattern:
- Remove ExecutionSettings component and any imports/references
- Remove global stdin/random_seed/attached_files state from CodeEditor
- Remove any hooks, context, or state management for global execution settings
- Remove related types if no longer referenced (e.g. ExecutionSettings interface)
- Audit for dead code paths that read/write global settings

## Relationship to other issues

- **PLAT-0xmt.6** (Trace debugging for test cases) overlaps on the per-case debug button for failed cases — this issue is broader, covering run + trace on all cases and the global UI removal.
- **PLAT-oztv** (Consolidate execution_settings) covers the data model unification — this issue is the frontend UX counterpart.
- Depends on PR 243 (PLAT-c6g6.3) landing first.

## Files likely affected

- `frontend/src/app/(fullscreen)/student/components/CasesPanel.tsx` — per-case run/trace buttons, run-all button
- `frontend/src/app/(fullscreen)/student/components/CaseResultDisplay.tsx` — action buttons per result
- `frontend/src/app/(fullscreen)/student/components/CodeEditor.tsx` — remove global execution settings panel and all related state
- `frontend/src/hooks/useCaseRunner.ts` — per-case run and trace methods
- Any ExecutionSettings component/type files — delete or gut

## Acceptance criteria

- Each test case has Run and Trace buttons
- "Run All" button executes all cases
- Global execution settings UI is gone
- No dead code from the old global execution settings pattern remains
- I/O-only problems with a single case feel as simple as the old global UI

description:
## Context

PR #219 (`feature/io-test-cases`, 145 files, 10,253 additions, 47 commits) has grown too large to land. It mixes two epics — PLAT-kh1h (I/O test cases) and PLAT-oztv (consolidate execution_settings) — into one monolith. Cherry-picking is impractical due to interleaved changes; each PR must be re-created from the branch's final file state.

There is an existing worktree at `/workspaces/eval-io-test-cases` with 8 uncommitted files (PLAT-xswh) that should be committed first to preserve work.

## Architecture Decisions

- **Single `/execute` endpoint** throughout — no separate `/student-work/{id}/test`. The old `test_execution.go` handler is dropped (YAGNI).
- **Frontend builds `Cases[]`** from `problem.test_cases` + student cases and sends to `/execute` directly. Server-side test loading can be added later if hidden test cases require it.
- **No compat layers in PR 1** — full-stack wire format change deployed as a single unit.
- **Small (~20 line) compat bridge in PR 2** — converts incoming `execution_settings` from old frontend to `IOTestCase[]` until PR 3 removes ExecutionSettings from frontend.

## Decomposition

| PR | Subtask | Description | ~Lines | Deploys After |
|----|---------|-------------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | PLAT-c6g6.1 | Execute protocol → Cases[] (executor + Go API + frontend) | 2,000 | Immediately |
| 2 | PLAT-c6g6.2 | Migrations + store refactor + iotestrunner | 3,000 | PR 1 |
| 3 | PLAT-c6g6.3 | Frontend IO test case UI + ExecutionSettings removal | 4,000 | PR 2 |

Total: ~9,000 lines across 3 deploy-safe PRs. Each subtask has detailed file lists, implementation steps, and acceptance tests.

## Execution Strategy

For each PR, branch from main and extract files from `origin/feature/io-test-cases`:
```bash
git checkout -b feature/<pr-name> main
git checkout origin/feature/io-test-cases -- <files>
# Adjust as needed (e.g., PR 1 executor doesn't use iotestrunner yet)
```

**Existing PR 219**: Close after all 3 PRs land, or repurpose.

## Key Wire Format Change (PR 1)

Before (flat):
```json
{"code": "...", "stdin": "...", "files": [...], "random_seed": 42}
→ {"success": true, "output": "...", "error": "", "execution_time_ms": 45}
```

After (Cases[]):
```json
{"code": "...", "language": "python", "cases": [{"name": "run", "input": "...", "files": [...], "random_seed": 42}]}
→ {"results": [{"name": "run", "status": "run", "actual": "...", "time_ms": 45}], "summary": {"total": 1, "run": 1}}
```

## Reviewer Notes

- PR 1 executor handler (per-case sandbox calls) is intentionally throwaway — PR 2 replaces with iotestrunner
- `executor/internal/config/config.go` must be updated when removing MaxStdinBytes/MaxFiles/MaxFileBytes
- `TraceRequest` in `pkg/executorapi/types.go` remains unchanged (debugger use)
- PR 2: verify whether existing `test_cases` JSONB has old TestCase[] data; confirm python3-pytest is needed; SessionPublisher interface signatures must change
- All tasks exceed 5-file sizing guideline but splitting creates awkward boundaries — accepted

title: Consolidate execution_settings into test cases
description:
Unify execution_settings and test cases into a single model. Every code execution is "run one or more test cases." ExecutionSettings (stdin, random_seed, attached_files) becomes fields on a test case. The separate execution_settings columns are removed.

BRANCH: feature/io-test-cases (PR #219). Use the existing worktree at /workspaces/eval-io-test-cases. Do NOT create a new branch — commit directly to feature/io-test-cases. Do NOT look at main — work from this branch.

Key decisions:
- Single /execute endpoint takes cases[] array. Response is always {results[], summary}.
- Cases without expected_output get status "run" (not "passed").
- Every problem/student_work always has at least one test case (DB-level NOT NULL + default).
- Migration converts existing execution_settings to a single default test case.
- sessions.featured_execution_settings → featured_test_cases (same pattern, carries test cases).

title: Migration: class_memberships table + RLS updates
description:
## Summary

Create the class_memberships table for class-level instructor roles. Update RLS policies so problems are class-scoped (not namespace-scoped) and section creation requires class membership. Migrate existing data.

## Files to modify

- New migration file: `migrations/020_class_memberships.up.sql` (and corresponding .down.sql)

## Files to read for context

- `migrations/001_initial_schema.up.sql` — problems table, sections table, section_memberships table, existing RLS functions (is_section_instructor, is_instructor_or_higher, is_section_member). Note how is_section_instructor accesses section_memberships — the same pattern should work for class_memberships.
- `migrations/015_section_problems_namespace_admin.up.sql` — can_manage_section() function, current RLS policies
- `migrations/019_class_scoped_problems.up.sql` — class_id is now NOT NULL on problems (from Epic 1)

## Implementation steps

1. Create `class_memberships` table:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE class_memberships (
     id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
     user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
     class_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES classes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
     role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('instructor')),
     joined_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
     UNIQUE(user_id, class_id)
   );
   ```
2. Create `is_class_instructor(class_id_param UUID)` helper function. **Important:** Use `SECURITY DEFINER` to avoid RLS recursion — this function is called from RLS policies on other tables, so it must bypass RLS on class_memberships:
   ```sql
   CREATE FUNCTION is_class_instructor(class_id_param UUID) RETURNS boolean AS $$
     SELECT EXISTS (
       SELECT 1 FROM class_memberships
       WHERE class_id = class_id_param
         AND user_id = app_user_id()
         AND role = 'instructor'
     );
   $$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER;
   ```
3. Enable RLS on class_memberships with policies:
   - SELECT: own memberships, or class members (via is_class_instructor), or namespace admins, or system admins
   - INSERT: class instructors (can add others) + namespace/system admins
   - DELETE: class instructors + namespace/system admins (last-member constraint enforced at app level)
   - **Note:** class_memberships SELECT policy must NOT call is_class_instructor to avoid recursion. Use a direct subquery check instead.
4. Migrate data — add class_memberships for:
   - Class creators: `INSERT INTO class_memberships (user_id, class_id, role) SELECT created_by, id, 'instructor' FROM classes`
   - Existing section instructors: `INSERT INTO class_memberships (user_id, class_id, role) SELECT DISTINCT sm.user_id, s.class_id, 'instructor' FROM section_memberships sm JOIN sections s ON s.id = sm.section_id WHERE sm.role = 'instructor' ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`
5. Update `problems_select` RLS — replace namespace scope with class instructor + published access. **Keep namespace check on student path for safety:**
   ```sql
   DROP POLICY "problems_select" ON problems;
   CREATE POLICY "problems_select" ON problems
     FOR SELECT USING (
       is_system_admin()
       OR is_class_instructor(class_id)
       OR EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM section_problems sp
         WHERE sp.problem_id = problems.id
           AND is_section_member(sp.section_id)
       )
     );
   ```
6. Update `problems_insert` — require class instructor AND namespace match:
   ```sql
   DROP POLICY "problems_insert" ON problems;
   CREATE POLICY "problems_insert" ON problems
     FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (
       is_system_admin()
       OR (is_class_instructor(class_id) AND namespace_id = app_namespace_id())
     );
   ```
7. Update `problems_update` — allow class instructors:
   ```sql
   DROP POLICY "problems_update" ON problems;
   CREATE POLICY "problems_update" ON problems
     FOR UPDATE USING (
       is_system_admin() OR is_class_instructor(class_id)
     );
   ```
8. Update `problems_delete` — allow class instructors:
   ```sql
   DROP POLICY "problems_delete" ON problems;
   CREATE POLICY "problems_delete" ON problems
     FOR DELETE USING (
       is_system_admin() OR is_class_instructor(class_id)
     );
   ```
9. Update `sections_insert` — require class membership:
   ```sql
   DROP POLICY "sections_insert" ON sections;
   CREATE POLICY "sections_insert" ON sections
     FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (
       is_system_admin()
       OR (namespace_id = app_namespace_id() AND is_class_instructor(class_id))
     );
   ```
10. Create down migration

title: Executor build retag fails on workflow_dispatch (duplicate SHA tag)
description:
BODY="## Summary

The \`build-push-executor\` job fails when triggered via \`workflow_dispatch\` (or re-run on the same commit) because \`gcloud artifacts docker tags add\` tries to add a commit SHA tag that already exists. Moving an existing tag requires \`artifactregistry.tags.delete\` permission, which the WIF service account lacks.

## Root Cause

The retag step (line 70-78 of \`.github/workflows/deploy-pipeline.yaml\`) runs unconditionally on cache hit:

\`\`\`yaml
- name: Retag existing image (cache hit)
  if: env.CACHE_HIT == 'true'
  run: |
    gcloud artifacts docker tags add \\
      \$REGISTRY/executor:content-\$CONTENT_HASH \\
      \$REGISTRY/executor:\${{ github.sha }}
\`\`\`

When the same commit SHA was already tagged (from a prior push-triggered run), this becomes a tag move, not a tag add, requiring \`tags.delete\` permission.

The comment on lines 76-78 already acknowledges this issue for \`:latest\` but doesn't handle the commit SHA tag case.

## Fix

Check if the SHA tag already exists before attempting the retag:

\`\`\`yaml
- name: Retag existing image (cache hit)
  if: env.CACHE_HIT == 'true'
  run: |
    # Check if SHA tag already exists (e.g. workflow_dispatch re-run)
    SHA_EXISTS=\$(gcloud artifacts docker tags list \$REGISTRY/executor \\
      --filter=\"tag:\${{ github.sha }}\" \\
      --format=\"value(tag)\" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -z \"\$SHA_EXISTS\" ]; then
      gcloud artifacts docker tags add \\
        \$REGISTRY/executor:content-\$CONTENT_HASH \\
        \$REGISTRY/executor:\${{ github.sha }}
    else
      echo \"SHA tag already exists, skipping retag\"
    fi
\`\`\`

## Files

- \`.github/workflows/deploy-pipeline.yaml\` lines 70-78

## Error

\`\`\`
PERMISSION_DENIED: Permission 'artifactregistry.tags.delete' denied on resource
'//artifactregistry.googleapis.com/.../executor/tags/d28a312e75b148b159a0a4876f518991dc63a0d0'
\`\`\`

https://github.com/jdelfino/eval/actions/runs/22693038864"

## Summary
`POST /api/v1/execute` currently wraps the new unified executor protocol behind a
legacy compat shim: it accepts `{code, language, stdin}`, synthesizes a single
`CaseDef{name:"run"}` with no expected output, sends it to the executor, then
converts the `{results[], summary}` response back to the old `{success, output,
error, execution_time_ms, stdin}` shape. This creates two divergent execution
paths in the frontend with different response types, different state, and different
UI rendering.

## Goal
Make `/api/v1/execute` speak the real protocol end-to-end. Remove the shim.

## Steps

1. **go-backend `handler/execute.go`**: Remove the legacy request/response types
   (`executeRequest`, `legacyExecuteResponse`). Accept `{code, language, cases[]}`
   natively and return `{results[], summary}` directly (same shape as
   `/student-work/{id}/test`).

2. **frontend `src/lib/api/execute.ts`**: Update `executeCode()` return type from
   `ExecutionResult` to `TestResponse`. Remove the `ExecutionResult` return path.

3. **frontend `student/page.tsx` `handleRunCode`**: Pass `instructorCases` to
   `executeCode()`. Handle the `TestResponse` result — either fold it into
   `caseRunner` state or replace `handleRunCode` + `useCaseRunner` with a single
   unified execution path.

4. **frontend `CodeEditor.tsx`**: Remove the `execution_result` display branch in
   the output area. All results flow through `CaseResultDisplay`.

5. **Types**: Retire `ExecutionResult` from `src/types/api.ts` if no longer used.

## Note
`POST /student-work/{id}/test` and `POST /sessions/{id}/test` remain as-is — they
are useful because they fetch cases server-side from the DB rather than requiring
the frontend to transmit case definitions. The executor unification (PLAT-oztv.2)

avoid touching the frontend during that phase.

title: Create ImpersonateContext, API functions, and header injection
Create impersonate handler and wire routes in server.go
description:
Create the HTTP handler for starting/stopping impersonation and wire it into the server middleware chain.

## Summary
Add API endpoints for entering and exiting impersonation, and wire the ImpersonateMiddleware into server.go in the correct position (after UserLoader, before PreviewMiddleware).

## Files to modify
- `go-backend/internal/handler/impersonate.go` — **New file**: handler with Routes()
- `go-backend/internal/handler/impersonate_test.go` — **New file**: handler tests
- `go-backend/internal/server/server.go` — Wire impersonate routes + middleware

## Files to read for context
- `go-backend/internal/handler/preview.go` — Reference handler pattern (Routes(), EnterPreview, ExitPreview)
- `go-backend/internal/handler/preview_test.go` — Reference test patterns
- `go-backend/internal/server/server.go` — Current middleware chain and route mounting (lines 186-220)
- `go-backend/internal/auth/permissions.go` — PermImpersonate permission (from task 1)
- `go-backend/internal/auth/context.go` — ImpersonateContext and CanImpersonate (from task 1)
- `go-backend/internal/middleware/impersonate.go` — ImpersonateMiddleware (from task 1)
- `go-backend/internal/store/interfaces.go` — UserReader interface

## Implementation steps

1. **Create `handler/impersonate.go`**:
   ```go
   type ImpersonateHandler struct {
       userReader store.UserReader  // pool-level, no RLS
   }
   
   func NewImpersonateHandler(userReader store.UserReader) *ImpersonateHandler
   ```

   **Routes()** method:
   ```go
   func (h *ImpersonateHandler) Routes() chi.Router {
       r := chi.NewRouter()
       r.Use(custommw.RequirePermission(auth.PermImpersonate))
       r.Post("/{userId}", h.EnterImpersonation)
       r.Delete("/", h.ExitImpersonation)
       return r
   }
   ```

   **POST /{userId} — EnterImpersonation**:
   a. Parse `userId` UUID from URL param
   b. Get authenticated admin from context
   c. Look up target user by ID via `h.userReader.GetUserByID()`; 404 if not found
   d. **Authorization**: Call `auth.CanImpersonate(admin, target)` — shared function from task 1
   e. **Audit log**: `slog.InfoContext(r.Context(), "impersonation started", "admin_id", admin.ID, "target_id", target.ID, "target_role", target.Role)`
   f. Return 200 with target user profile. Handle nullable NamespaceID (dereference with empty string fallback — safe since only non-system-admin users can be impersonated):
      ```json
      {
        "id": "uuid",
        "email": "user@example.com",
        "role": "student",
        "namespace_id": "ns-id",
        "display_name": "User Name"
      }
      ```

   **DELETE / — ExitImpersonation**:
   a. Get authenticated admin from context
   b. **Audit log**: `slog.InfoContext(r.Context(), "impersonation ended", "admin_id", admin.ID)`
   c. Return 204 No Content

2. **Wire in `server.go`** (insert between UserLoader and Preview routes):
   ```go
   // After JWT + UserLoader (line 193), before preview routes (line 196):
   
   // Impersonate routes: mounted before ImpersonateMiddleware so they use
   // the real admin identity. These routes only need JWT + UserLoader.
   if pgxPool := pool.PgxPool(); pgxPool != nil && userStore != nil {
       impersonateUserReader := store.New(pool.PgxPool())
       impersonateHandler := handler.NewImpersonateHandler(impersonateUserReader)
       r.Mount("/system/impersonate", impersonateHandler.Routes())
       
       // ImpersonateMiddleware: swaps user identity when X-Impersonate-User
       // header is present. MUST be before PreviewMiddleware so impersonation
       // takes precedence and preview POSTs are blocked by read-only mode.
       r.Use(custommw.ImpersonateMiddleware(impersonateUserReader))
   }
   
   // ... existing preview routes and middleware follow ...
   ```

   **Critical ordering note:** In Chi v5, `r.Mount()` before `r.Use()` means the mounted routes are NOT affected by the middleware. This is the same pattern as preview routes (mounted in a Group before PreviewMiddleware's `r.Use()`). The impersonate routes (POST enter, DELETE exit) bypass the ImpersonateMiddleware, so the admin's real identity is used and POST/DELETE are not blocked by read-only enforcement.

3. **Write handler tests** in `impersonate_test.go`:
   - EnterImpersonation: valid target → 200 with user profile
   - EnterImpersonation: target not found → 404
   - EnterImpersonation: target has equal role → 403 (via CanImpersonate)
   - EnterImpersonation: namespace-admin targets user in different namespace → 403
   - EnterImpersonation: invalid UUID → 400
   - ExitImpersonation: returns 204
   - Routes: permission gate blocks students/instructors

   Use mock UserReader with function fields (same pattern as preview_test.go).

## Testing notes
Unit tests for handler. Additionally, add an **integration-style test** that verifies the middleware ordering is correct: send `DELETE /system/impersonate` with both an `Authorization` header (valid admin JWT) AND an `X-Impersonate-User` header → must return 204, NOT 403 read-only. This validates the fragile route/middleware ordering.

title: Add PermImpersonate, ImpersonateContext, and ImpersonateMiddleware
description:
Add the backend auth primitives and middleware for user impersonation.

## Summary
Create the permission, context helpers, and middleware that enable admins to impersonate users. The middleware intercepts `X-Impersonate-User` header requests, swaps the authenticated user's identity to the target user, and enforces read-only mode by rejecting non-safe HTTP methods.

## Files to modify
- `go-backend/internal/auth/permissions.go` — Add `PermImpersonate` permission, grant to `namespace-admin` and `system-admin` roles
- `go-backend/internal/auth/context.go` — Add `ImpersonateContext` struct, `WithImpersonateContext()`, `ImpersonateContextFrom()`, `IsImpersonating()` helpers; add `CanImpersonate()` shared validation function
- `go-backend/internal/middleware/impersonate.go` — **New file**: ImpersonateMiddleware
- `go-backend/internal/middleware/impersonate_test.go` — **New file**: middleware tests
- `go-backend/internal/auth/permissions_test.go` — Update permission matrix tests

## Files to read for context
- `go-backend/internal/middleware/preview.go` — Reference implementation for identity-swap middleware pattern
- `go-backend/internal/middleware/preview_test.go` — Reference for test patterns
- `go-backend/internal/auth/context.go` — Existing PreviewContext pattern to follow
- `go-backend/internal/auth/permissions.go` — Current permission/role definitions
- `go-backend/internal/store/interfaces.go` — `UserReader` interface (lines 492-507) used by middleware
- `go-backend/internal/middleware/authz.go` — RequirePermission pattern

## Implementation steps

1. **Add `PermImpersonate` permission** to `permissions.go`:
   - Add constant: `PermImpersonate Permission = "impersonate.enter"`
   - Add to `rolePermissions` map for `RoleNamespaceAdmin` and `RoleSystemAdmin`

2. **Add `ImpersonateContext`** to `context.go`:
   ```go
   type ImpersonateContext struct {
       OriginalUser *User  // The admin who initiated impersonation
   }
   ```
   - Add `impersonateContextKey` to context keys
   - Add `WithImpersonateContext(ctx, ic)`, `ImpersonateContextFrom(ctx)`, `IsImpersonating(ctx)` helpers
   - Follow the exact same pattern as `PreviewContext` (lines 51-106)

3. **Add shared `CanImpersonate` function** to `context.go` (or a new `impersonate.go` file in the auth package):
   ```go
   // CanImpersonate checks whether impersonator can impersonate target.
   // Returns nil if allowed, or an error describing why not.
   func CanImpersonate(impersonator, target *User) error
   ```
   - **Role guard**: Block if target role >= impersonator role. Use ordering: student < instructor < namespace-admin < system-admin. Specifically:
     - namespace-admin can impersonate student, instructor
     - system-admin can impersonate student, instructor, namespace-admin
     - Return error "cannot impersonate user with equal or higher role" if blocked
   - **Namespace guard** (for namespace-admin only): Verify `target.NamespaceID == impersonator.NamespaceID`; return error if mismatch
   - Both the middleware and handler will call this shared function to avoid duplication

4. **Create `middleware/impersonate.go`**:
   - Constructor: `ImpersonateMiddleware(userReader store.UserReader) func(http.Handler) http.Handler`
   - The middleware uses a pool-level `UserReader` (no RLS) to look up target users, same pattern as preview middleware using pool-level `previewStore`
   - Logic:
     a. Check for `X-Impersonate-User` header; pass through if absent
     b. Get authenticated user from context; 401 if missing
     c. **Defense-in-depth**: Check `auth.IsImpersonating(ctx)`; if true, return 403 "nested impersonation is not allowed"
     d. Check `auth.HasPermission(user.Role, auth.PermImpersonate)`; 403 if denied
     e. Parse target user UUID from header; 400 if invalid
     f. **Read-only enforcement**: If HTTP method is not GET, HEAD, or OPTIONS → return 403 with body `{"error": "impersonation mode is read-only"}`
     g. Look up target user by ID via `userReader.GetUserByID()`; 404 if not found
     h. **Authorization**: Call `auth.CanImpersonate(impersonator, target)` — returns role guard and namespace guard errors
     i. Build impersonated `auth.User` from the target user record
     j. Swap identity: `ctx = auth.WithUser(ctx, targetUser)`
     k. Preserve original: `ctx = auth.WithImpersonateContext(ctx, ImpersonateContext{OriginalUser: impersonator})`
     l. **Disable preview**: If `X-Preview-Section` header is also present, strip it (impersonation takes precedence)
     m. **Audit log**: `slog.InfoContext(ctx, "impersonation active", "admin_id", impersonator.ID, "target_id", targetUser.ID, "target_role", targetUser.Role)`
     n. Call `next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))`

5. **Write tests** in `impersonate_test.go`:
   - No header → pass-through (no-op)
   - Student tries to impersonate → 403
   - Instructor tries to impersonate → 403
   - Namespace-admin impersonates student in same namespace → identity swapped
   - Namespace-admin impersonates instructor in same namespace → identity swapped
   - Namespace-admin impersonates user in different namespace → 403
   - Namespace-admin impersonates another namespace-admin → 403
   - System-admin impersonates any non-system-admin → identity swapped
   - System-admin impersonates system-admin → 403
   - Invalid UUID header → 400
   - Target user not found → 404
   - POST request during impersonation → 403 read-only
   - PUT request during impersonation → 403 read-only
   - GET request during impersonation → passes through
   - ImpersonateContext preserved in context after swap
   - X-Preview-Section header stripped during impersonation
   - Already-impersonating context → 403 nested impersonation blocked

6. **Update `permissions_test.go`** to include `PermImpersonate` in the permission matrix assertions.

## Testing notes
Unit tests only for this task. The middleware tests should use mock `UserReader` (function field pattern matching existing handler test mocks). Also add unit tests for `CanImpersonate()` covering all role combinations and namespace scenarios.

description:

Motivation: Without style references, each generated problem has inconsistent formatting. Instructors have their own conventions — rather than prescribing a format, learn it from examples.

How it works:
- ProblemIntake gains an optional StyleReferences []string field (paths to prior problem READMEs or statement text)
- When provided, the system prompt includes the reference problems with an instruction: "Match the structure, section ordering, tone, and formatting conventions of these reference problems. Do not copy content — only match the format."
- When absent, the engine generates with its default structure (no change from current behavior)

Progressive enhancement:
- First problem for a course: no references available, engine picks a reasonable structure
- Instructor edits the output to their preferred style
- Subsequent problems: prior output becomes the style reference, format converges naturally

This is lightweight — no new data model, just prior problem text included in the prompt alongside the constraint block.

title: Integration bridge — constraint injection into problemgen
description:
Wire the course model into the problem gen engine (PLAT-qli) as an optional input. This is the integration point.

Changes to problemgen:
1. ProblemIntake gains optional fields:
   CourseModelPath string  // path to YAML file (optional)
   TargetUnitID   string  // which unit this assignment targets (optional)

2. When CourseModelPath is provided:
   a. Load the course model via coursemodel.Load()
   b. Derive constraints via coursemodel.DeriveConstraints(model, targetUnitID)
   c. Format via coursemodel.FormatForPrompt(constraints)
   d. Inject formatted constraint text into the system prompt

3. When absent: engine behaves exactly as before (graceful degradation)

Files to modify:
- problemgen/engine.go — accept optional course model, load + derive constraints in Start()
- problemgen/system_prompt.go — inject constraint text block into system prompt

Key: the constraint text is injected as hard rules, not suggestions. The system prompt must treat available/forbidden knowledge as absolute constraints.

CRITICAL PROMPT ENGINEERING NOTE (from manual testing):
Forbidden knowledge must be framed as "does not exist," not "do not use." When constraints say "don't use len()" the LLM will helpfully tell students "solve this without using len()" — which introduces len() to students who have never heard of it. The correct framing:

  FORBIDDEN KNOWLEDGE — these concepts DO NOT EXIST in the student's world.
  Do not mention them, do not warn against them, do not say "without using X."
  If a concept is not in the available knowledge list, it simply does not exist.
  The student has never heard of it. Write as if it was never invented.

This "doesn't exist" framing prevents the LLM from leaking forbidden concepts through helpful prohibitions. Apply this principle to all generated output: problem statement, starter code, solution comments, test names, and hints.

API:

  AddMaterial(ctx, CourseMaterial) — ingests text/PDF, LLM proposes/updates timeline
  Chat(ctx, message) — freeform conversation for refinement
  Model() — returns current CourseModel state
  Save() — writes YAML to output path

  set_prerequisites(prerequisites[]) — set/update prerequisite knowledge
  add_unit(id, name, description?) — add a unit to the timeline
  update_unit(id, name?, description?) — modify existing unit

  finalize() — mark model as ready for review

- Analyze uploaded materials to identify course structure
- Propose timeline conservatively — less detail initially, instructor requests more
- Never invent content not evidenced in materials or stated by instructor
- Support coarse granularity (just units) and fine (concepts, objectives)

description:
Implement DeriveConstraints(model, targetUnitID) and FormatForPrompt(constraintSet). This is the most novel and valuable piece — it translates a structured course model into actionable LLM constraints.

- AvailableKnowledge = prerequisites + timeline[0..N] (inclusive)
- ForbiddenKnowledge = timeline[N+1..]
- ConceptSummary = flattened concept names from available units
- AssessedSkills = assessments matching available units/concepts (empty initially)

FormatForPrompt() renders the constraint set as a text block for injection into an LLM system prompt:
  COURSE CONTEXT: CS 201 (Python)
  AVAILABLE KNOWLEDGE: ...
  FORBIDDEN KNOWLEDGE: ...
  CONSTRAINTS: problem MUST be solvable with available knowledge only, do NOT use forbidden concepts

- Coarse model (no concepts): works with unit-level only

- Assessment filtering: only includes assessments for available knowledge

- FormatForPrompt: renders readable, well-structured text

title: PR preview environments (deferred)
description:
**STATUS: Deferred.** The env-up/env-down primitives from PLAT-xhxf.1 make this easy to add later. This plan needs additional vetting before implementation — the scope (nginx ingress, wildcard DNS, cert-manager, orphan GC, IDP domain config) is significant and there's no immediate user for preview environments.

---

On-demand PR preview environments with browser access, triggered by adding a label to a PR.

## UX Flow

1. Developer opens PR, pushes code. PR CI runs normally.
2. Developer or reviewer adds label `preview` to PR.
3. GitHub Actions triggers preview-env.yaml:
   a. Build images from PR branch, push as $REGISTRY/<service>:pr-<number>
   b. Run env-up.sh --namespace pr-<number>
      - Creates namespace pr-<number>
      - Creates database eval_pr_<number> on shared Cloud SQL instance
      - Deploys all services (go-api, frontend, centrifugo, redis, executor)
      - Runs migrations, seeds with test data
   c. Creates nginx Ingress for pr-<number>.preview.eval.delquillan.com
   d. Posts PR comment with preview URL

4. New pushes to PR while `preview` label is present:
   - Rebuild images, redeploy to same namespace (rolling update)
   - Post update comment: "Preview updated to <sha>"

5. PR merges, closes, or `preview` label removed:
   - kubectl delete ns pr-<number> (cascades all resources)
   - DROP DATABASE eval_pr_<number>
   - Post comment: "Preview environment torn down."

## Infrastructure needed

- Nginx ingress controller (Helm chart) — single LB shared across all previews (~$3/mo)
- Wildcard DNS record: *.preview.eval.delquillan.com → nginx ingress LB IP
- SSL: cert-manager with Let's Encrypt, or skip SSL for preview environments
- IDP: add *.preview.eval.delquillan.com to authorized_domains, use test tenant
- Orphan GC: scheduled workflow to clean up namespaces older than 48h

## API endpoints

### Assignment management (instructor)
- POST   /api/assignments                            — Create assignment
- GET    /api/assignments                            — List assignments (query param: class_id). RLS ensures students only see published+released assignments for their sections.
- GET    /api/assignments/{id}                       — Get assignment
- PATCH  /api/assignments/{id}                       — Update assignment
- DELETE /api/assignments/{id}                       — Delete assignment

### Section assignment management (instructor)
- POST   /api/assignments/{id}/sections              — Release to section (create section_assignment with optional due_at, released_at)
- GET    /api/assignments/{id}/sections              — List section assignments for this assignment
- PATCH  /api/assignments/{id}/sections/{sectionId}  — Update section config (due_at, released_at)
- DELETE /api/assignments/{id}/sections/{sectionId}  — Remove from section

### Student actions
- POST   /api/assignments/{id}/start                 — Start assignment (creates repo + workspace, returns workspace URL)
- GET    /api/assignments/{id}/workspace              — Get workspace URL for current student

Note: Students list their assignments via GET /api/assignments — RLS policies filter to show only assignments released to their enrolled sections.

## Start Assignment flow (POST /api/assignments/{id}/start)
1. Load assignment, verify status=published
2. Find student's section membership for the assignment's class
3. Verify section_assignment exists and released_at <= now
4. Check no existing student_assignment for this user+assignment (return existing workspace URL if found)
5. Create Gitea repo for student (fork source repo into student-named repo)
6. Create Coder workspace from template, passing repo_url parameter
7. Insert student_assignment record with repo_gitea_id, repo_url, workspace_id, workspace_name, status=in_progress, started_at=now
8. Return workspace access URL

## Error handling for Start Assignment
- If Gitea repo creation succeeds but Coder workspace fails: delete the orphaned Gitea repo, return error
- If DB insert fails after both external calls succeed: best-effort cleanup of Gitea repo + Coder workspace, return error
- Idempotency: if student_assignment already exists, return existing workspace URL instead of error

## Notes
- Follow existing store patterns: pgx queries, sentinel errors (store.ErrNotFound), pgx.Rows scanning
- Follow existing handler patterns: chi URL params, JSON request/response, auth.UserFromContext
- Gitea and Coder clients should be interfaces on the handler struct for testability (mockable)

title: Test generation — system prompt + hidden/public test tools
description:
The crown jewel. Engineer the system prompt and tool definitions for generating comprehensive, high-quality test suites.

IMPORTANT DESIGN CHANGE: The engine generates ONE unified test suite, not separate public/hidden suites. Visibility (which tests students can see) is a pedagogical decision made by the instructor after generation, not by the engine. The engine's tools should be updated accordingly:
- Replace write_public_tests / write_hidden_tests with a single write_tests tool
- Each test can optionally have a category tag (structural, basic-correctness, edge-case, performance, common-mistake) to help instructors make visibility decisions, but the engine does NOT assign visibility

Files to modify:
- problemgen/system_prompt.go — test generation guidance in the system prompt
- problemgen/tools.go — replace dual test tools with single write_tests tool

System prompt must encode expertise about writing a SINGLE comprehensive suite:

1. Structural tests:
   - Code compiles / imports correctly
   - Expected class/function names exist with correct signatures
   - Correct parameter types and return types
   - These catch the 'silly' mistakes every student makes

2. Basic correctness tests:
   - Happy path with simple, representative inputs
   - Examples from the problem description
   - Clear, descriptive test names

3. Edge case tests:
   - Boundary values, empty input, single element
   - Corner cases specific to the algorithm
   - Large inputs for performance (when O complexity matters)

4. Common-mistake tests:
   - Off-by-one errors, wrong base case, mutation of input
   - Bugs specific to the problem domain

Test quality principles:
   - ONE BUG PER TEST: each test targets exactly one specific bug. The test's docstring must document which bug it catches and how that bug manifests. If you can't name the specific bug, the test is too vague.
   - DOCUMENTED: every test function has a docstring stating (a) the specific bug it targets, and (b) what incorrect behavior it would catch. This documentation helps instructors understand each test's purpose when deciding visibility.
   - NO REDUNDANCY: each test must catch a distinct bug. Self-check: "if a student passes test A, could they still fail test B?" If not, one is redundant. Remove it.
   - Test BEHAVIORS, not format decomposition. Don't break one exact-match check into 10 substring checks — that's the same assertion repeated with worse error messages.
   - Descriptively named: test name explains the specific scenario (e.g. test_empty_list_returns_none, not test_edge_case_1)
   - Independent: tests don't depend on each other's state
   - Deterministic: no randomness, no timing-dependent assertions
   - Robust: not brittle to valid alternative implementations

CRITICAL — COURSE MODEL CONSTRAINT AWARENESS:
When a course model is provided, tests must also respect the knowledge boundary:
- Test names must not reference forbidden concepts (the "doesn't exist" principle)
- Tests should target mistakes students make WITH THE AVAILABLE TOOLS, not mistakes involving forbidden concepts
- If a concept isn't in the student's world, it shouldn't appear in test names, comments, or error messages

Target: pytest for Python. Test files should be runnable with 'pytest tests/ -v'.

Acceptance criteria:
  1. Generate 3 sample problems (beginner, intermediate, advanced)
  2. For each, verify:
     - At least 1 structural test
     - At least 3 basic correctness tests
     - At least 3 edge case / common mistake tests
     - All test names describe the specific scenario
     - Every test has a docstring documenting the single bug it targets
     - NO redundant tests (apply the "could they pass A but fail B?" check)
  3. Run validation: solution passes all tests
  4. Spot-check: manually introduce a common bug and verify at least one test catches it
  5. When course model constraints are provided, verify no test references a forbidden concept

This task is primarily prompt engineering — the code changes are small but the prompt content is critical. Expect iteration.

title: Unify local and CI build tooling (eliminate Make/CI mismatch)
description:
## Summary
The Makefile is used for some local tasks (build, test, lint, docker-build) but CI workflows duplicate the same commands in GitHub Actions YAML. This creates a maintenance burden where changes must be made in two places, and CI behavior can drift from local behavior.

## Problem
Examples of duplication:
- `make test-api` runs `go test -race ./...` — go-api.yaml also runs `go test -v -race ./...` (different flags)
- `make lint-api` runs `golangci-lint run ./...` — go-api.yaml uses `golangci-lint-action@v4`
- `make docker-build-api` builds with `go-backend/` as context — go-api.yaml builds with `.` as context and `-f go-backend/Dockerfile`
- Frontend CI has no `docker-build-frontend` make target, while go-api and executor do

The Makefile is incomplete (missing `docker-build-frontend`) and CI doesn't use it, so adding to one doesn't fix the other.

## Options to evaluate
1. **Make CI use Makefile targets** — CI steps become `make test-api`, `make lint-api`, etc. Single source of truth. But some CI-specific needs (caching, actions) may not fit.
2. **Remove Makefile, use scripts/** — Each task gets a script (`scripts/test-api.sh`), CI and local both call it. More explicit.
3. **Use a task runner** (just, taskfile, etc.) — Modern alternative to Make with better cross-platform support.
4. **Accept the duplication** — Document it and move on. Pragmatic but accumulates drift.

## Action items
- Decide on approach
- Implement chosen solution
- Ensure `docker-build-frontend` works identically locally and in CI

title: Upgrade beads from v0.49.1 to latest Dolt-backed release
description:
Upgrade beads (bd) from v0.49.1 to the latest stable Dolt-backed release (currently v0.57.0, but wait for stability).

## Why

The SQLite+JSONL backend we're on is no longer maintained. The Dolt backend provides:
- Cell-level merge (vs line-level JSONL conflicts)
- Shared database across git worktrees (instant visibility, no stale copies)
- Better concurrent write support (server mode)
- Sync via existing GitHub repo using git+ssh:// remote (refs/dolt/data)

## When to pull the trigger

Wait until 2-3 consecutive releases without major Dolt backend fixes (transaction isolation, schema re-init, batch commit races). As of v0.57.0 the fix rate is still high -- check release notes before upgrading.

## Migration steps

1. bd export -- save current issues as JSONL backup
2. Upgrade bd binary (brew, mise, or install script)
3. bd init -- re-initializes with Dolt backend
4. bd dolt remote add origin git+ssh://git@github.com/jdelfino/eval.git
5. bd dolt push -- initial push to GitHub
6. Update AGENTS.md -- replace bd sync with bd dolt push / bd dolt pull
7. Remove sync-branch from .beads/config.yaml
8. Optionally enable auto-push in config (dolt.auto-push: true)
9. Verify: bd list, bd ready, bd dolt pull from a fresh clone
10. Remove legacy .beads/beads.db and JSONL sync artifacts

## Files to update

- .beads/config.yaml -- remove sync-branch, add dolt config
- AGENTS.md -- replace bd sync references
- CLAUDE.md -- update bd commands if needed
- Devcontainer setup if bd install method changes

## Risks

- Data loss during migration (mitigated by JSONL export backup)
- git+ssh:// remote is new (Feb 2026) -- may have rough edges
- Dolt server auto-start may need devcontainer adjustments

title: Fix executor scale-to-zero: deploy GMP frontend, configure KEDA properly
description:
## Summary

The executor KEDA ScaledObject is configured with minReplicaCount: 0, but scale-to-zero doesn't work due to three issues. Currently set to minReplicaCount: 1 as a workaround (~$11/mo cost).

## Problems to fix

1. **No GMP query frontend deployed** — The ScaledObject references `http://frontend.gmp-system.svc:9090` but this service doesn't exist. GKE Managed Prometheus collects metrics but doesn't deploy an in-cluster query frontend by default. Deploy the frontend Deployment+Service in gmp-system namespace per GCP docs.

2. **KEDA ignoreNullValues** — When executor has 0 replicas, no pods emit `executor_active_executions`. KEDA 2.16.1 treats missing metrics as TriggerError (default ignoreNullValues: true). Add `ignoreNullValues: "false"` to the ScaledObject trigger metadata so KEDA treats missing metrics as 0.

3. **Scale-from-zero trigger** — Even with 1+2 fixed, KEDA can't scale FROM zero because the metric is only emitted by executor pods. Options:
   - Add a Redis queue depth metric from go-api (preferred — already uses Redis for rate limiting)
   - Add a KEDA cron trigger for business hours
   - Use a KEDA webhook/HTTP trigger from go-api's submission endpoint

## Files to modify

- k8s/base/executor-scaledobject.yaml — Add ignoreNullValues, potentially add second trigger for scale-from-zero
- k8s/base/gmp-frontend.yaml — New file, deploy GMP query frontend (Deployment + Service)
- k8s/base/kustomization.yaml — Add gmp-frontend.yaml

## Current workaround

minReplicaCount: 1 in executor-scaledobject.yaml. The executor node pool always has 1 node running (~$11/mo spot).

title: E2E Auth Testing Infrastructure
description:
## Summary
Set up infrastructure for end-to-end testing of registration and authentication flows, including email verification.

## Scope
- Email receiving service for tests to read verification codes
- Test utilities for Cognito user lifecycle
- E2E tests covering: registration → email verification → login → token refresh

## Email Service Options (verify free tiers)

| Service | Free Tier | Notes |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| **Mailtrap** | 100 emails/month | Likely sufficient for E2E |
| **testmail.app** | 100 emails/month | Simple API |
| **Mailosaur** | Free trial only | No permanent free tier (~$10/mo) |
| **Ethereal** | Unlimited | Fake SMTP, good for dev, not real delivery |

**Recommendation:** Start with Mailtrap or testmail.app (free tier), switch if limits are hit.

## Test Cases
1. **Registration flow:** Sign up → receive email → extract code → verify → login
2. **Password reset:** Forgot password → receive email → extract code → reset → login
3. **Token refresh:** Login → wait → refresh token → verify still authenticated

## Implementation Notes
- Use Cognito Admin APIs for test setup/teardown (create users, clean up)
- Email service only needed for the `extract verification code` step
- Consider running full E2E sparingly (nightly) vs admin-bypass tests in CI

## Dependencies
- Requires working Cognito setup (PLAT-dar)
- Requires Go API auth endpoints (PLAT-nqj)

## Future Work
- SAML flow testing (requires mock IdP)
